assets.prompt:
Generate exactly ONE standalone 16:9 horizontal Chinese article illustration, ideally 1536x864. Use case: illustration-story; mature sparse absurd editorial ink sketch for a technical article, NOT a slide.
Pure #FFFFFF white background with no paper texture, no shadows, no gradients, no noise. Slightly wobbly fine black hand-drawn ink outlines, large quiet margins and at least 40% empty white space. Sparse tiny handwritten Chinese labels next to objects, no title, no top-left heading, no legend, no PPT grid, no infographic boxes, no polished vector art, no commercial illustration, no children’s cartoon.
The central actor is XiaoM (小M), serious deadpan little mushroom doing the conceptual work: red dome mushroom cap with 3–5 WHITE dots, cream stem with black outline, tiny BLACK dot eyes, thin black arms and legs, no clothes, no smile, not a cute mascot. Include only 1–2 thin ORANGE mycelium threads serving the action. Red is mostly the mushroom cap; annotations may use restrained orange/blue/red. All scene and text safely within the central 85% of canvas.
Anchor01, Sandbox versus Supervisor. Draw a low-tech isolated workshop as a spare cutaway room at left center, enclosing XiaoM actually working at a small bench, handling a tool and a workpiece. The room has continuous solid walls, one single narrow exit at its RIGHT wall, and no other opening. A completely SEPARATE trusted gatekeeper, a plain tall black-outline mechanical figure, stands physically OUTSIDE the room to the right. Its arm operates the external latch on the ONLY exit. XiaoM has no access to this latch. A single thin orange mycelium/request thread from the bench reaches the sole exit and stops for inspection by the gatekeeper; no bypass path. This should read as an odd little workshop with an outside warden, with natural irregular perspective and much white air. Room = execution, external gatekeeper = authorization. No key props in this first picture.
Only these handwritten labels, correctly drawn beside their actual objects: "隔离工作间" beside room; "Sandbox" small below that; "唯一出口" beside the single opening; "门外审批" beside the separate gatekeeper; "Supervisor" small beneath gatekeeper label. No other text. Do not imply the Sandbox itself is trusted to authorize its own escape.

Anchor03, three independent permission-check outcomes. ONE XiaoM sits at a plain spare inspection desk, actively testing THREE physical permission slips fanned out unevenly across the desk. A low crooked black boundary hoop is the tangible test gauge, not a flowchart. The first slip fits INSIDE the boundary hoop and has a GREEN hand-drawn checkmark plus handwritten "边界内" and tiny "读 /usr". The second slip visibly protrudes OUTSIDE the hoop: a RED rejection X, handwritten "越界" and concrete counterexample "反例：写 /tmp". The third slip has an unresolved folded / tangled end, a large ORANGE question mark and handwritten "无法证明"; it remains ON THE DESK, not admitted and has NO green check. XiaoM is holding and examining that third uncertain slip through a simple magnifying glass, blank serious eyes. A single thin orange mycelium curls from XiaoM’s foot to that slip, serving the inspection action. Three slips with distinct outcomes are the only colorful results; no fourth slip, no panels, no table, no UI.
Small handwritten caution near the uncertain slip, verbatim: "无法证明 ≠ 通过". This is a verdict about a policy checker, NOT proof of whole-system security. Use exactly these sparse short labels only. Green for the successful result ONLY, red for the violated boundary ONLY, orange for unsupported uncertainty. Keep all three outcomes visible and distinct in a mature, loose, absurd ink scene with plenty of pure white space.
